chapter: Tom Brown's band and the first Dixieland claim
title: Bill Lambert's letter on Brown's band and La Rocca's angry response
summary: Lambert's 1936 letter recalls Brown's band in Chicago and Hoboken around 1915. La Rocca, calling Lambert Brown's drummer, denounces historians, defends his compositions and says Dixieland started name bands and arrangements.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: This is dated New Orleans, Louisiana, 10-21-36. Dear friend Nick, received your letter and was very glad to hear from you. Was glad to hear that you are in good health. as this letter leaves me the same. Was also glad to hear that you are doing good and hope you will continue to do so. If I remember correctly, the building of the band when we were in Chicago playing at the Lambs Cafe was Brown's Band from Dixieland. We opened an engagement there on a short time after May the 15th. Sorry I'm not able to furnish you with any exact dates as all the clippings I had... ... ...

destroyed by fire since returning home we were built at a theater in Hoboken New Jersey as Brown's band Kings of Ragtime that was during the latter part of 1915 I think also played an engagement at the Century Theater in New York and played Lowe's it says Lowe's time as the musical rules give my regards to Larry Tony and any of the other boys I know my wife sends her best regards wishing you the best of luck and success I remain your friend Bill Lambert

that is a drummer of Brown's band now you historians all his turns including the great mr. Sushant go look up and see if you see any building of them but you're willing to print that they were the first original Dixieland jazz band you're not only about to be ashamed of yourself you should go to the top of the new bridge and jump off that's where you belong because if you were around this person as you say you're intelligent you have an education which I have not got but I have more truth in my little finger than you got in your whole body you have lied to the people you have told them truths I'm not suffer by it you will and miss men will go down she deserted to sink and ship after I sent her a few letters that will go down in history if the honor scholar will listen to my letters they'll know what they did to me around New Orleans they're not only persecuted me you mean little of me there's not a man ever lived since the time of Jesus Christ that they put so much lies against for what I never know they say I was trying to take the credit for everything now if you were leader of a band and you were out there before others and you know they didn't play that you wouldn't see Al Jolson say that Eddie Cantor was Al Jolson no that's different but me I'd have to say they did play what I did to say that they did play what I did to say. I played nine oh they're liars I'm not gonna say it because I'm gonna tell the truth they didn't play what I played the fact is it's not only one number that I compose but I have about 20 of them published already and I got at least 30 of them home and I can make another thousand before I die if I want them right now because I know how to compose it too I know how to arrange it they didn't have that they didn't have that and that was the beginning what we did was the beginning of all name bands came special arrangements came all what you want but the Dixieland showed the way original Dixieland. Dixieland I want to come to a part where we played the St. Louis Blues of course this will bring me back into 1920 again but this is the only way I can get it on as I come to these things.
